Posted April 7, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan
You have perhaps heard that Canada, like the EU and Mexico, does not have a death penalty, and that, like The Netherlands, it has a medical cannabis program.
See
 MarijuanaNews Reported It A Month Ago, But Now It's Official: Dutch Pharmacies Provide Medical Cannabis Covered by Health Insurance.

Wrong on both counts. It is true that Canada does not execute even mass-murderers, and it is true that it is under court order to provide patients with a legal source of medical cannabis, but right now MichaelPatriquen is being slowly murdered in a Canadian prison by a government that refuses to obey its own laws.
See
 Ontario Judge Prods Canadian Government On Medical Cannabis Program. Supreme Court Hearings On All Cannabis Prohibition Now Set For May. We Are Winning!

He is wasting away with nausea from untreated pain. In late March, he said, " This has been going on for six months and I'm very weak from it. I lost 39 pounds because of my inability to eat since the time of my sentencing on Sept. 10. "

Now consider this story:
From Hour Magazine
letters@afterhour.com
http://www.hour.ca/
By Charlie McKenzie
March 20, 2003
MARIJUANA IN JAIL? NEVER!

It's common knowledge that drugs are readily available in Canada's prisons - unless you have a prescription. Michael Patriquen, leader of Nova Scotia's Marijuana party and past federal candidate, has a doctor's prescription and a Health Canada permit for medicinal marijuana to help with chronic pain stemming from a 1999 car accident. But he's also serving a six-year prison sentence for various marijuana offences and Corrections Canada has a strict 'no way' policy about handing out marijuana to prisoners.

" There is still no legal supply ( of marijuana ) available, " explained prison spokeswoman Lynn Chaplin.

They offered Patriquen synthetic THC pills but he refused on the advice of other doctors.
(MarijuanaNews note: Marinol lacks the other cannabinoids that help reduce pain as well as moderating the psychoactivity of the THC.)
See
 Gettman Petition For Hearings On Marinol Rescheduling Uses DEA's Own Arguments Against It.
Why Marinol Is Not Medical Marijuana. Wonderfully Brilliant!
and
 DEA Says THC Is Safe. "! As The Volume Of Prohibitionist Propaganda Goes Up, The Quality Goes Down. Drug Czar Makes A Fool of Himself In Maryland. DEA Now Sending Emails Against Medical Cannabis.

Another prison doctor offered opiates, which he also refused. " I told him that I didn't want a drug problem on top of everything else. They're highly addictive. "

So Patriquen is doing something relatively novel: He's taking his jailor to court. The case has drawn the attention of millionaire marijuana activist Marc Emery, who will help bankroll the action. Emery has provided major funding for almost every pro-pot effort in North America, including numerous court challenges. One is heading for the Supreme Court later this spring, which could remove Canada's marijuana prohibition altogether.

John Conroy of Abbotsford, B.C., an expert in cannabis and penal law, has been hired to handle Patriquen's case. In the late '60s Conroy founded the Canadian chapter of the National Organization for the Reform of Marijuana Laws (NORML).
(MarijuanaNews note: Conroy is also counsel for the BC Compassion Society.)
See
 Canadian Supreme Court Punts On Cannabis Cases Until Spring. The Games Governments Play Prove The Need for International Debate on Cannabis Prohibition. Special to MarijuanaNews

Senator Pierre Claude Nolin, who wants marijuana legalized, says Patriquen's rights are being ignored. " He's entitled to get marijuana no matter where he is in Canada, " Nolin says.
(MarijuanaNews note: Senator Nolin is speaking on April 18th at the NORML conference in San Francisco and will be on the panel that I am chairing.)

Canada's Solicitor-General Wayne Easter disagrees. " We don't want to go down that route... if you are in prison you're not there to smoke marijuana, " he said.

That's for the court to decide.
Copyright: 2003, Communications Voir Inc.
(MarijuanaNews note: Easter is a party-line prohibitionist, so he necessarily has a hard time with the facts. Patriquen doesn't smoke cannabis. He eats it.

They would be happy for him to eat Marinol, which has only the psychoactive THC, but not the other cannabinoids, which are not psychoactive, and help control the psychoactivity of the THC.

But it gets even worse, and the truth is even more embarrassing for the Canadian government, and for me, too.

Health Canada has a legal supply of medical cannabis. You may have heard of Prairie Plant System's medical marijuana mine in Flin Flon, Manitoba
See
 Health Canada Gives $5.7 Million Contract to Company With No Experience to Grow Mediocre Weed for Medical Marijuana Research

When Steve Tuck fled to Canada in June of 2001, he donated 15,000 medical cannabis seeds, of 400 different varieties, to Health Canada for use by Prairie Plant Systems in Flin Flon, Manitoba, which has a contract to provide Health Canada with medical cannabis. These seeds were the source of the first successful crop harvested by PPS. That crop of 74 kilograms, delivered in December of 2001, contained 185 different varieties that Tuck gave them.

Unfortunately, Health Canada chose to use this wide variety of plants as an excuse not to use the resulting crop, and at one point, they even said they were going to burn it.

Subsequently, they have said that it will be used in research.

When this story first came out, I knew about Tuck's seeds, but I foolishly took Health Canada at its word that these seeds had been confiscated by the police.
See
Blame DEAland: Canadian Health Minister Blames DEA for Canadian Medical Cannabis Fiasco. DEA Wouldn't Sell Them Seeds. Now If Someone In Canada Would Go Into The Seed Business

That was only technically true. I should have wondered how would they know how many varieties the police had seized...

Actually, Tuck presented the seeds to be seized, since that was the only legal way that Health Canada could take them. I missed the real story.

It will be presented to the Canadian court by Conroy in Tuck's affidavit for Patriquen.

Under cannabis prohibition, government stealing is legal, but accepting a gift from an expert is illegal.

The inversion of morality and the refusal to recognize anyone who actually knows something about the plant is inherent in the suppression of medical cannabis.
See
 Canadian Health Minister Seeks Asylum In DEAland; Says Making Her Think About Medical Cannabis Constitutes Torture. In DC They Don't Allow That Sort of Thing. Thinking, That Is.

However, in December of 2002, Prairie Plant Systems delivered a second crop of 200 kilograms based on the two or three best strains from the first crop. Thus, Health Canada has available to it a wide variety of medical grade cannabis suitable for use by patients, including Patriquen.

In fact, Tuck, who suffers from pain and nausea like Patriquen, developed the strains to deal with precisely such problems, and Patriquen, who ingests his cannabis would be a perfect test subject for the various strains.
See
 In Their Own Words: FDA Press Release On New Anti-Nausea Drug For Chemotherapy Patients Prove Prohibitionists Are Lying About Need For Medical Cannabis.

Such research is even legal under the UN/DEAland treaties.
See
Swiss Government Says Going Dutch Does NOT Violate Treaties. Implications for Other Countries, Especially Canada and UK. Plus Full Text of UN Nark Press Release.

So the Canadian government is breaking its own laws that require that it give prisoners the best available medicine.

The incredible irony is that Steve Tuck, who is a medical cannabis refugee from DEAland, gave it to them.

So, they are lying about not having a legal source of medical cannabis, and Michael Patriquen is being slowly and painfully murdered. Or should I say, Executed eh?

We couldn't make this up!)

and
